about: THE OLD WAYS - real sailing directions of the period cut into legs (from, the words, the bearing as the text has it, the days, the landmarks, where scholars place the end). Laid out on the map with the dividers; sailing near an end finds it. Made by Bake/guide/make_chest_data.py from Plans/environment_research/m3/sailing.json.

from.name: Ohthere's home in northernmost Hálogaland (the Malangen-Lenvik area south of Tromsø is the usual placing (?))

to.name: the whale-hunters' furthest point (no agreed place; set here off Sørøya, ours (?))

legs.original: Þa for he norþryhte be þæm lande: let him ealne weg þæt weste land on ðæt steorbord, ⁊ þa widsæ on ðæt bæcbord þrie dagas. Þa wæs he swa feor norþ swa þa hwælhuntan firrest faraþ.
legs.translation: Then he went right north near the land: he left, all the way, the waste land on the right, and the wide sea on the left, for three days. Then was he as far north as Whale-hunters ever go.
legs.landmarks: waste land to starboard (steorbord), open sea to port (bæcbord); ends at the furthest point the whale-hunters reach
legs.scholars: All agree he followed the Norwegian coast north-east. Where the whale-hunters stopped is not known; any point between Tromsø and Sørøya fits (?).

to.name: North Cape (Nordkapp) or Nordkinn, where the coast turns east

legs.original: Þa for he þagiet norþryhte swa feor swa he meahte on þæm oþrum þrim dagum gesiglan. Þa beag þæt land þær eastryhte, oþþe seo sǽ in on ðæt lond, he nysse hwæðer
legs.translation: He then went yet right north, as far as he could sail in the next three days. Then the land bent there right east, or the sea in on the land, he knew not whether
legs.days: on þæm oþrum þrim dagum (in the next three days)
legs.landmarks: the land turns east (or the sea runs into the land; he did not know which)
legs.scholars: Most place the turn at the North Cape or Nordkinn, the north tip of Norway. Fairly sure.

to.name: where the land turns south: Svyatoy Nos, the east tip of the Kola peninsula, at the mouth of the White Sea (usual placing)

legs.original: buton he wisse ðæt he ðær bád westanwindes ⁊ hwon norþan, ⁊ siglde ða east be lande swa swa he meahte on feower dagum gesiglan. Þa sceolde he ðær bidan ryhtnorþanwindes, for ðæm þæt land beag þær suþryhte, oþþe seo sǽ in on ðæt land, he nysse hwæþer.
legs.translation: but he knew that he there waited for a western wind, or a little to the north, and sailed thence east near the land, as far as he could sail in four days. Then he must wait there for a right north wind, because the land bent there right south, or the sea in on the land, he knew not whether.
legs.landmarks: land still to starboard; at the end the land turns south
legs.scholars: Most: the turn into the White Sea at Svyatoy Nos (Kola). A minority keep him inside Varangerfjord or along the Kola coast. Fairly sure, not certain. 644 km in 4 days is fast for day-sailing, which some use to argue a shorter run (?).

to.name: a great river: the Northern Dvina mouth (traditional; Bosworth 1859, Malte-Brun) where the game's Bjarmaland stands

legs.original: Þa siglde he þonan suðryhte be lande swa swa he mehte on fíf dagum gesiglan. Ða læg þær án micel ea up in on þæt land.
legs.translation: Then sailed he thence right south, near the land, as far as he could sail in five days. There lay then a great river up into the land
legs.landmarks: land to starboard all the way, open sea ('á widsǽ') to port; a great river runs up into the land; the far bank is settled by the Beormas, so they dare not pass it
legs.scholars: Unsure. Older writers: the Northern Dvina. Many modern writers: a river on the Terskiy coast of Kola (Varzuga or Umba). The river is the edge of Beormas land either way.

to.name: Sciringes heal = Skíringssalr, the market at Kaupang, Vestfold

legs.original: Þonne is án port on suðeweardum þæm lande, þone man hæt Sciringes heal. Þyder he cwæð þæt man mihte geseglian on anum monðe, gyf man on niht wicode, ⁊ ælce dæge hæfde ambyrne wind; ⁊ ealle ða hwile he sceal seglian be lande. ⁊ on þæt steorbord him bið ærest Iraland, ⁊ þonne ða igland þe synd betux Iralande ⁊ þissum lande. Þonne is þis land oð he cymð to Scirincges heale, ⁊ ealne weg on þæt bæcbord Norðweg.
legs.translation: Then there is a port, on the south of the land [Norway], which is called Sciringesheal. Thither he said, that a man could not sail in a month, if he anchored at night, and every day had a fair wind. All the while he must sail near the land. — On his right hand, is first Iceland, and then the islands which are between Iceland and this land [Britain]. Then this land continues till he comes to Sciringesheal; and all the way, on the left, [is] Norway.
legs.bearing: none given; the port is 'on suðeweardum þæm lande' (in the south part of the land), so south is implied
legs.days: on anum monðe (in a month), camping each night with a fair wind every day. The Lauderdale MS says one COULD sail it in a month; the Cotton MS says one could NOT (see variant_readings).
legs.landmarks: always along the land; to starboard first Iraland, then the islands between Iraland and 'this land' (England); to port Norðweg (Norway) the whole way
legs.scholars: Sciringes heal = Kaupang in Tjølling, Vestfold: sure (Snorri's Skíringssalr; excavations). 'Iraland' is the MS reading (Ireland); Bosworth and Rask changed it to Iceland; most modern readers keep Ireland and take it loosely for the British Isles over the sea to starboard (?).

to.name: the south end of the Kattegat, at the mouth of the Great Belt by Sjællands Odde (ours (?))

legs.original: ⁊ of Sciringes heale he cwæð þæt he seglode on fíf dagan to þæm porte þe mon hæt æt Hæþum … Ða he þiderweard séglode fram Sciringes heale, þa wæs him on þæt bæcbord Denamearc, ⁊ on þæt steorbord widsǽ þry dagas
legs.translation: He said that he sailed in five days, from Sciringesheal to the port which they call Haddeby [near Schleswig] … When he sailed thitherward from Sciringesheal, then Denmark was on his left; and, on his right, a wide sea for three days
legs.days: þry dagas (three days), the first part of 'on fíf dagan' (five days) to æt Hæþum
legs.landmarks: Denamearc to port (bæcbord), open sea (widsǽ) to starboard
legs.scholars: Most read 'Denamearc' here as the Danish-ruled east side of the Kattegat (Viken, Halland, Skåne), so he kept the Swedish west coast to port. Where the three days end is not stated (ours (?)).

to.name: æt Hæþum = Hedeby (Haithabu) on the Schlei

legs.original: ⁊ þa, twegen dagas ær he to Hæþum come, him wæs on þæt steorbord Gotland, ⁊ Sillende, ⁊ iglanda fela. On þæm landum eardodon Engle, ær hi hider on land coman. ⁊ hym wæs ða twegen dagas on ðæt bæcbord þa igland þe in Denemearce hyrað.
legs.translation: and, the two days before he came to Haddeby, he had on his right, Jutland, Zealand, and many islands. The Angles dwelt in these lands, before they came into this country. And, these two days, the islands, which belong to Denmark, were on his left.
legs.landmarks: to starboard Gotland (= Jutland), Sillende and many islands; to port the islands that belong to Denmark. The Angles lived here before they came to England.
legs.scholars: æt Hæþum = Hedeby: sure. Route through the Great Belt (or the Little Belt) (?). 'Sillende' is south-east Jutland/Schleswig for many modern scholars, Zealand for Bosworth and Thorpe (?).

to.name: the gap between Rügen and Skåne, with Skåne to port (ours (?))

legs.original: Wulfstan sæde þæt he gefóre of Hæðum, þæt he wære on Truso on syfan dagum ⁊ nihtum, þæt þæt scip wæs ealne weg yrnende under segle. Weonoðland him wæs on steorbord, ⁊ on bæcbord him wæs Langaland, ⁊ Læland, ⁊ Falster, ⁊ Scóneg; ⁊ þas land eall hyrað to Denemearcan.
legs.translation: Wulfstan said that he went from Haddeby,—that he was in Truso in seven days and nights,—that the ship was running all the way under sail. He had Weonodland, [Mecklenburg and Pomerania] on the right [star-board,] and Langland, Laaland, Falster and Sconey, on his left, and all these lands belong to Denmark.
legs.days: part of 'on syfan dagum ⁊ nihtum' for the whole run
legs.landmarks: Weonoðland (the Wendish coast) to starboard; Langeland, Lolland, Falster, then Skåne to port (all Danish)
legs.scholars: Langaland, Læland, Falster, Scóneg = Langeland, Lolland, Falster, Skåne: sure. Course out of the Schlei, south of the Danish islands: likely.

to.name: south-east of Bornholm (ours (?))

legs.original: ⁊ þonne Burgenda land wæs us on bæcbord, ⁊ þa habbað him sylf cyning.
legs.translation: And then we had, on our left, the land of the Burgundians [Bornholmians], who have their own king.
legs.days: part of the seven days and nights
legs.landmarks: Burgenda land (Bornholm) to port; it has its own king
legs.scholars: Burgenda land = Bornholm: sure.

to.name: Wislemuða, the 'Vistula mouth' where the lagoon ran out to the sea 'west and north' (place unsure; set at the west end of the Vistula Spit, ours (?))

legs.original: Þonne æfter Burgenda lande wæron ús þas land, þa synd hatene ærest Blecingaég, ⁊ Meore, ⁊ Eowland, ⁊ Gotland on bæcbord; ⁊ þas land hyrað to Sweon. ⁊ Weonodland wæs ús ealne weg on steorbord oð Wislemuðan.
legs.translation: After the land of the Burgundians, we had, on our left, those lands that were called first Blekingey, and Meore, and Oeland and Gothland; and these lands belong to Sweden. And we had Weonodland, on the right, all the way to the mouth of the Vistula.
legs.days: part of the seven days and nights
legs.landmarks: Blekinge, Möre, Öland and Gotland to port (Swedish); Weonodland to starboard all the way to Wislemuða
legs.scholars: Blecingaég, Meore, Eowland, Gotland = Blekinge, Möre (Småland coast), Öland, Gotland: sure. Wislemuða: the Vistula's way to the sea; its exact 9th-century place is disputed (an outlet of the Vistula Lagoon, or the river mouth by Gdańsk) (?).

to.name: Truso, at Janów Pomorski on Lake Druzno near Elbląg

legs.original: ⁊ seo Wisle lið út of Weonodlande, ⁊ lið in Estmere; ⁊ se Estmere is huru fiftene mila brád. Þonne cymeð Ilfing eastan in Estmere of ðæm mere ðe Truso standeð in staðe
legs.translation: The Vistula flows out of Weonodland and runs into the Frische Haff [Estmere]. The Frische Haff is, at least, fifteen miles broad. Then the Elbing comes from the east into the Frische Haff, out of the lake [Drausen] on the shore of which Truso stands
legs.bearing: none; the Ilfing comes 'eastan' (from the east)
legs.days: part of the seven days and nights
legs.landmarks: across the Estmere (Vistula Lagoon, 'at least fifteen miles broad'), up the Ilfing (Elbląg river) to the mere (Lake Druzno) where Truso stands on the shore
legs.scholars: Estmere = Vistula Lagoon, Ilfing = Elbląg river, the mere = Lake Druzno: sure. Truso = the trading site excavated at Janów Pomorski since 1982: sure.

from.name: Brittania (the north of Britain; Dunnet Head used, ours)

to.name: Thile (Thule) = Iceland for Dicuil (south coast used, ours)

legs.original: Plinius Secundus in quarto libro edocet quod Pytheas Masiliensis sex dierum navigatione in septentrionem a Brittania Thilen distantem narrat.
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Dicuil takes Thule as the island his clerics visited, i.e. Iceland: sure. What Pytheas himself meant (Iceland, Norway or Shetland) is disputed, but not needed here.

to.name: the sea-ice (congelatum mare), north of Iceland (no fixed place; ours)

legs.original: sed navigatione unius diei ex illa ad boream congelatum mare invenerunt.
legs.translation: and that a day's sail towards the north would bring them from thence into the frozen sea.
legs.landmarks: the clerics stayed from 1 February to 1 August; light enough at midnight to pick lice from a shirt; the frozen sea one day further north
legs.scholars: The drift-ice edge north of Iceland: sure in kind, not a fixed place. Its distance changes with the year; the game could tie it to the season.

from.name: the northern islands of Britain (Shetland; Unst used, ours)

to.name: the Faroes (Tórshavn used)

legs.original: Sunt aliae insulae multae in septentrionali Brittaniae oceano, quae a septentrionalibus Brittaniae insulis duorum dierum ac noctium recta navigatione plenis velis assiduo feliciter vento adiri queunt.
legs.translation: there are many other islands in the northern British sea, which lie at the distance of two days and two nights from the northern islands of Britain, in a straight course, and with a fair wind and a full sail.
legs.bearing: recta navigatione (a straight run), no compass word
legs.days: duorum dierum ac noctium (two days and nights), full sails, a steady fair wind
legs.landmarks: small islands parted by narrow sounds, full of sheep and sea-birds; Irish hermits lived there for nearly a hundred years until the Norse raiders emptied them
legs.scholars: The Faroes: sure (narrow sounds, sheep = Færeyjar). Anderson 1873 took these first islands for Shetland; most now do not.

from.name: not stated (the northern isles of Britain implied)

to.name: one of the Faroes

legs.original: aliquis presbyter religiosus mihi retulit quod in duobus aestivis diebus et una intercedente nocte navigans in duorum navicula transtrorum in unam illarum introivit.
legs.translation: "One of these," he says, "a certain honest monk told me he had visited one summer after sailing a day, a night, and another day, in a two-benched boat."
legs.days: in duobus aestivis diebus et una intercedente nocte (two summer days and the night between)
legs.landmarks: a small boat with two thwarts (duorum navicula transtrorum)
legs.scholars: One of the Faroes: likely. Shows a small open boat could make the crossing in summer.

to.name: Iumne = Wolin at the Oder mouth

legs.original: nam per mare navim ingrederis ab Sliaswig vel Aldinburc, ut pervenias ad Iumne.
legs.days: none by sea (by land from Hamburg or the Elbe: 'septimo die', the seventh day)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Iumne = Wolin: sure.

to.name: Ostrogard Ruzziae: Rus; taken here as Novgorod (Holmgarðr) by way of the Gulf of Finland, the Neva, Ladoga and the Volkhov (?)

legs.original: Ab ipsa urbe vela tendens quartodecimo die ascendes ad Ostrogard Ruzziae. Cuius metropolis civitas est Chive, aemula sceptri Constantinopolitani, clarissimum decus Graeciae.
legs.bearing: none ('ascendes': you go up, i.e. upriver at the end)
legs.landmarks: the last part goes 'up' (ascendes): a river
legs.scholars: Ostrogard (Old Norse Austrgarðar) is Rus in general; the river end is most likely Novgorod or Ladoga (?). Adam's own note makes Kiev its chief city.

from.name: Dania (the Danish islands; the Sound used, ours)

to.name: Ostrogard Ruzziae (Novgorod used (?))

legs.original: Affirmant autem Dani, longitudinem huius ponti saepe a pluribus expertam, secundo flatu per mensem aliquos a Dania pervenisse in Ostrogard Ruzziae.
legs.bearing: none (the Baltic runs 'versus orientem', eastward, Schol. 115)
legs.days: per mensem (in a month), secundo flatu (with a following wind)
legs.landmarks: the whole length of the Baltic
legs.scholars: As leg 2. A month against Wolin's fourteen days: two measures that do not agree.

from.name: Alaburc, promunctorium Daniae (Lappenberg: Skagen, the tip of Vendsyssel)

to.name: the south Norwegian skerries (Agder/Vestfold coast, ours (?))

legs.original: cuius ab oceano introitus inter Alaburc, promunctorium Daniae, scopulosque Nortmanniae tam strictus invenitur, ut facili saltu per noctem carbasa traiciantur.
legs.days: per noctem (in one night); IV 1: 'Inde brevissimus in Nordmanniam transitus est' (from Wendila the shortest crossing to Norway)
legs.landmarks: the rocks of Norway (scopulos Nortmanniae)
legs.scholars: Skagen to the Norwegian coast is about 130-160 km: a night and a day's edge. Fits.

to.name: Wig: Lappenberg's note: not a town but the bay 'Wigen' near Tønsberg, the land called Vík (Viken)

legs.original: Est vero iter eiusmodi, ut ab Alaburg vel Wendila Danorum ingredientibus navim per diem mare transeatur ad Wig, civitatem Nortmannorum
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Wig = Vík, the Oslofjord region, landing near Tønsberg: likely.

to.name: Trondemnis = Niðaróss (Trondheim)

legs.original: inde vela torquentur in laevam, circa littora Norvegiae; quinta die pervenitur ad ipsam civitatem quae Trondempnem dicitur.
legs.bearing: in laevam (to the left: a turn, not a compass point)
legs.landmarks: round the coasts of Norway
legs.scholars: Trondemnis = Trondheim: sure. 1,078 km in five days is very fast; days and nights at sea are implied (?).

to.name: Orchades (Orkney; Birsay used)

legs.original: Ad quas a civitate Nortmannorum Trondemni per diem ferunt navigari posse.
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Orkney: sure. 'One day' is impossible for ~870-900 km; Adam reports hearsay ('ferunt').

to.name: Anglia (England; Lindisfarne used as the first English landfall, ours)

legs.original: Itemque ab Orchadibus, aiunt, simile spatium viae, sive in Angliam dirigas, sive in Scotiam flectere velis.
legs.days: simile spatium viae (the same length of way, i.e. a day)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Hearsay; a day reaches north Scotland, not England.

to.name: Island (Iceland; Eyrar used)

legs.original: Egredientibus a promunctorio Danorum Alaburg narrant iter esse 30 dierum usque in Island, minus autem, si ventum habeant secundum.
legs.days: iter esse 30 dierum (a journey of 30 days); less with a following wind
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Iceland: sure. Thirty days is a whole season's average with waiting for wind.

from.name: a littore Nortmannorum (the Norwegian coast; Stad used, ours)

to.name: Gronland (Greenland; Brattahlíð used)

legs.original: Ad quam ferunt insulam a littore Nortmannorum vela pandi quinque aut septem diebus, quemadmodum ad Island.
legs.days: quinque aut septem diebus (in five or seven days), the same as to Iceland
legs.landmarks: Greenland lies 'deeper in the ocean, opposite the mountains of Sweden or the Riphaean range'
legs.scholars: Greenland: sure. 5-7 days fits Norway to Iceland (compare Landnámabók: seven dœgr Stad to Horn), not Greenland.

from.name: Britannia (north Britain; Dunnet Head used, ours)

to.name: Thyle = Island (Iceland, south coast used)

legs.original: Quod fieri in insula Thyle, Pytheas Massiliensis scribit sex dierum navigatione in septentrionem a Britannia distante. Haec itaque Thyle nunc Island appellatur, a glacie quae occeanum astringit.
legs.days: sex dierum navigatione (six days' sailing); Schol. 147: 'A qua novem dierum navigatione pervenitur ad Thile' (nine days)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Adam names Thule as Iceland: sure (his own words).

to.name: mare congelatum (the sea-ice; ours)

legs.original: De qua unius diei navigatio est ad mare congelatum.
legs.landmarks: Schol. 149: 'Iuxta Island est oceanus glaciatus et fervens et caligans' (by Iceland the ocean is frozen, seething and dark)
legs.scholars: Same as Dicuil leg 2.

from.name: Sconia Danorum (Skåne; south coast used, ours)

to.name: Sictona (Sigtuna) or Birca (Birka), close together in Lake Mälaren

legs.original: Est vero iter eiusmodi, ut a Sconia Danorum per mare velificans quinto die pervenias usque Sictonam vel Bircam, iuxta enim sunt. Si vero per terram eas a Sconia per Gothorum populos et civitatem Scaranem, Telgas et Bircam, completo mense pervenies Sictonam.
legs.days: quinto die (on the fifth day); Schol. 121: 'navigantibus ad Bircam quinque dierum' (five days to Birka). By land: completo mense (a full month).
legs.landmarks: none at sea; the land road goes by Skara and Telge
legs.scholars: Sigtuna and Birka: sure. A land-or-sea choice: five days by sea against a month by land, good for the route planner.

to.name: Ruzzia: Rus (Aldeigjuborg on the Volkhov used (?))

legs.original: a Birca in Ruzziam similiter per mare habes iter quinque dierum.
legs.days: iter quinque dierum (a journey of five days)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: 'Russia' could mean the Gulf of Finland shore or Ladoga; unsure (?).

to.name: Cincfal (Sincfal), the old inlet of the Zwin by Bruges (Lappenberg thought it a Maas mouth)

legs.original: De Ripa in Flandriam ad Cincfal velificari potest duobus diebus et totidem noctibus
legs.bearing: angulosus inter austrum et occidentem (slanting between south and west), said of the whole run Ribe-Prol
legs.days: duobus diebus et totidem noctibus (two days and as many nights)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Cincfal = the Zwin estuary (Sincfal) near Bruges: likely.

to.name: Prol = Prawle Point, Devon (Lappenberg)

legs.original: de Cincfal ad Prol in Angliam duobus diebus et una nocte. Illud est ultimum caput Angliae versus austrum, et est processus illuc de Ripa angulosus inter austrum et occidentem.
legs.bearing: angulosus inter austrum et occidentem (between south and west)
legs.days: duobus diebus et una nocte (two days and one night)
legs.landmarks: Prol is 'ultimum caput Angliae versus austrum' (the southernmost cape of England)
legs.scholars: Prawle Point: likely (Lappenberg's note).

to.name: Sanctus Mathias = Pointe Saint-Mathieu, Brittany

legs.original: De Prol in Britanniam ad Sanctum Mathiam uno die
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Saint-Mathieu (St Mahé): sure.

to.name: Far: A Coruña (the Farum Brigantium lighthouse) or Ferrol (Lappenberg) (?)

legs.original: inde ad Far iuxta Sanctum Iacobum tribus diebus et tribus noctibus.
legs.bearing: processus iste angularis totus inter austrum et occidentem (this whole stretch slants between south and west), said of Prol to Lisbon
legs.landmarks: near Santiago (iuxta Sanctum Iacobum)
legs.scholars: Lappenberg: Ferrol. The name 'Far' (pharos) suits A Coruña's Roman lighthouse (?).

to.name: Leskebone = Lisbon

legs.original: Inde ad Leskebone duobus diebus et duabus noctibus, et est processus iste angularis totus inter austrum et occidentem.
legs.bearing: angularis totus inter austrum et occidentem (between south and west)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Lisbon: sure.

to.name: Narvese = the Strait of Gibraltar (Old Norse Njörvasund)

legs.original: De Leskebone ad Narvese tribus diebus et tribus noctibus, angulariter inter orientem et austrum.
legs.bearing: angulariter inter orientem et austrum (between east and south)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Gibraltar strait: sure (Lappenberg).

to.name: Arrugun (Arragun) = Tarragona

legs.original: De Narvese ad Arrugun quatuor diebus et quatuor noctibus, angulariter inter aquilonem et orientem.
legs.bearing: angulariter inter aquilonem et orientem (between north and east)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Tarragona: likely (Lappenberg).

to.name: Barzalun = Barcelona

legs.original: De Arragun ad Barzalun uno die similiter inter aquilonem et orientem.
legs.bearing: similiter inter aquilonem et orientem (likewise between north and east)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Barcelona: sure.

to.name: Marsilia = Marseille

legs.original: De Barzalun ad Marsiliam uno die et una nocte, fere versus orientem, declinando tamen parum ad plagam australem.
legs.bearing: fere versus orientem, declinando tamen parum ad plagam australem (nearly east, a little to the south); 100 is ours
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Marseille: sure. The text's 'east, a little south' is wrong by about 50° (true course north-east): a trap.

to.name: Mezcin = Messina, Sicily

legs.original: De Marsilia ad Mezcin in Sicilia quatuor diebus et quatuor noctibus, angulariter inter orientem et austrum.
legs.bearing: angulariter inter orientem et austrum (between east and south)
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Messina: sure.

to.name: Accharon = Acre (Akko)

legs.original: De Mezcin ad Accharon 14 diebus et totidem noctibus inter orientem et austrum, magis appropiando ad orientem.
legs.bearing: inter orientem et austrum, magis appropiando ad orientem (between east and south, nearer east); 112 is ours
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Acre: sure (Lappenberg: St Jean d'Acre).

to.name: Anglia (the Humber/Lindsey coast used, ours (?))

legs.original: Ad Angliam faventibus euris vela pandis.
legs.landmarks: IV 1: Ribe's river 'per quem vela torquentur in Fresiam, aut certe in Angliam vel in nostram Saxoniam' (by which sails turn to Frisia, England or our Saxony)
legs.scholars: A wind rule, not a distance. Ties to the weather model: an easterly is the day to leave Ribe for England.

from.name: ostium Wirrahae (the Weser mouth), 'a litore Fresonum'

to.name: Orchades (Orkney)

legs.original: eo quod ab incolis eius populi dicitur ab ostio Wirrahae fluminis directo cursu in aquilonem nullam terram occurrere praeter infinitum occeanum. … Deinde relinquentes hinc Daniam, inde Britanniam, pervenerunt ad Orchadas.
legs.bearing: directo cursu in aquilonem (straight course to the north)
legs.landmarks: Denmark on one side, Britain on the other
legs.scholars: Told to Adam by Archbishop Adalbert of a voyage in his predecessor's time (Alebrand, 1035-1043) (?).

to.name: Island (Iceland; Horn, the usual east landfall, used)

legs.original: Quibus a laeva dimissis, cum Nordmanniam in dextris haberent, longo traiectu glacialem Island collegerunt.
legs.bearing: none (sides: Orkney left astern to port, Norway to starboard)
legs.landmarks: Orkney to port, Norway to starboard
legs.scholars: Iceland: sure. The voyage then goes on into the dark frozen sea and a whirlpool (not a leg).

to.name: Thíle = Ísland (the prologue says wise men take Iceland for Thule)

legs.original: ok er sagt at liggi sex dœgra sigling norðr frá Bretlandi.
legs.translation: which in books is said to be six days' sailing north from Britain.
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: From Bede's De temporum ratione (725), itself from Pliny/Pytheas. Thule = Iceland in the saga writers' view.

to.name: Horn on the east of Iceland (Eystrahorn / Vesturhorn by Höfn)

legs.original: Svá segja vitrir menn, at ór Noregi frá Staði sé sjau dœgra sigling í vestr til Horns á austan-verðu Íslandi.
legs.translation: So wise men say, that from Norway, out of Stad, there are seven half-days' sailing to Horn, in eastern Iceland
legs.days: sjau dœgra sigling (seven dœgr); Ellwood: 'seven half-days'; Origines: 'seven days' [24 hours']'
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Staðr = Stad: sure. Horn = the Horn headlands of south-east Iceland: likely.

from.name: Snjófjallz-nes / Snæfellsnes, west Iceland (the tip used)

to.name: Hvarf in Greenland (Hauksbók) / the east coast of Greenland (Sturlubók). Hvarf: near Cape Farewell (?)

legs.original: En frá Snjófjallz-nesi þar sem skemst er, er fjogurra dœgra sigling til Hvarfs á Grœnalandi.
legs.translation: and from Snowfells Ness, where the cut is shortest, there is four days' main west to Greenland.
legs.bearing: none in Hauksbók; Sturlubók and Ellwood: 'í vestr' (west)
legs.landmarks: none; 'þar sem skemst er' (where it is shortest)
legs.scholars: Four dœgr fits the short crossing to East Greenland (~650 km), not Hvarf (~1,170 km). The two texts disagree; let the player find out.

from.name: Hernar, islands off Hordaland north-west of Bergen (?)

to.name: north of Shetland (ours)

legs.original: Af Hernum af Noregi skal sigla jamnan í vestr til Hvarfs á Grœnalandi; ok er þá siglt fyrir norðan Hjaltland; svá at því at eins sé þat, at all-góð sé sjóvar-sýn
legs.translation: From Horn [sic: Hernar] from Norway one must sail ever west to Wharf [Farewell] in Greenland, and then the course sailed is north of Shetland, within sight of land, if there be a very clear day
legs.landmarks: pass north of Hjaltland (Shetland), seen only when the sea-view is very good
legs.scholars: Hernar = the Hernar islands (Hordaland): accepted; exact islet (?). The Hauksbók clause is called Haukr's own addition (Prose Reader notes).

to.name: south of the Faroes (ours)

legs.original: en fyrir sunnan Færeyjar, svá at sjór er í miðjum hlíðum
legs.translation: and south of Faereys, so that the sea be half-way up the slopes
legs.landmarks: pass south of the Faroes so far that the sea cuts their slopes halfway (they show half sunk below the horizon)
legs.scholars: A sight-distance rule: the Faroes' height half over the horizon puts you some 50-60 km off (ours (?)).

to.name: off south Iceland (ours)

legs.original: en svá fyrir sunnan Ísland, at þeir hafa af fugl ok hval.
legs.translation: and so to the south of Iceland, so as to get to [that distance from the coast, where you meet] the fowl and whales.
legs.landmarks: south of Iceland, close enough to have its birds and whales, not its coast
legs.scholars: A bird-and-whale sign, not a sighting: likely the edge of the Iceland shelf (ours (?)).

to.name: Hvarf, near Cape Farewell (Hvarfsgnípa) (?)

legs.original: til Hvarfs á Grœnalandi
legs.translation: to Wharf [Farewell] in Greenland
legs.days: none (Adam IV 36: Norway to Greenland 'quinque aut septem diebus')
legs.landmarks: Hvarf, the turning-point headland at Greenland's south end
legs.scholars: Hvarf: the southern tip region of Greenland where ships turned north-west to the Eastern Settlement; exact headland (?).

from.name: Björgyn (Bergen) — Sturlubók only; founded c. 1070, after the game

to.name: Hvarf (?)

legs.original: En sva er sagt, ef siglt er or Biorgvin rétt í vestr til Hvarfsins á Grœnlande, at þá man siglt vera tylft fyrir sunnan Ísland.
legs.translation: But it is said, that if one sail from Bergen straight west to Warf, in Greenland, then one must keep about 12 miles (sea miles) south of Iceland
legs.landmarks: 'tylft' (a twelve) of sea-miles south of Iceland
legs.scholars: Same course as legs 4-7, from Bergen. Out of the game's years unless used for Hernar.

to.name: Jöldu-hlaup ('Mare's leap') in Ireland: unidentified headland; north-west Ireland used (Malin Head, ours (?))

legs.original: Frá Reykja-nesi á sunnan-verðu Íslandi er þriggja dœgra haf til Jöldu-hlaups á Írlandi í suðr
legs.translation: but from Reekness, in southern Iceland, there is five days' main to Jolduhlaup, in Ireland, going south
legs.days: þriggja dœgra haf (three dœgr of sea), Hauksbók; five in Sturlubók/Ellwood; 'eight [MS. three]' in Origines 1905
legs.landmarks: none
legs.scholars: Jölduhlaup is not identified. Ireland lies south-east of Reykjanes, not south: the Icelandic compass skew again. 1,270 km makes three dœgr impossible; Vigfusson's 'eight' tries to mend it.

to.name: Svalbarði ('cold edge'): Jan Mayen used (?); East Greenland or Spitsbergen also proposed

legs.original: en frá Langa-nesi á norðan-verðu Íslandi er fjogurra dœgra haf til Svalbarða norðr í Hafs-botn
legs.translation: but from Longness, in northern Iceland, there is four days' main north to Svalbard, in Hafsbotn
legs.days: fjogurra dœgra haf (four dœgr of sea)
legs.landmarks: Hafsbotn, 'the sea's bottom', the Arctic ice-bay
legs.scholars: Not identified. Jan Mayen fits four dœgr (~570 km); Spitsbergen does not.

from.name: Kolbeins-ey (Kolbeinsey), the rock north of Iceland

to.name: the wastes of East Greenland (Scoresby Sund side used, ours (?))

legs.original: en dœgr-sigling er til óbygða á Grœnalandi ór Kolbeins-ey í norðr.
legs.translation: but one day's sail there is to the Wastes of Greenland from Kolbein's Isle in the north.
legs.landmarks: the uninhabited wastes (óbygðir) of Greenland
legs.scholars: Kolbeinsey: sure. The Greenland coast is north-west, ~300 km: far more than one dœgr (?).

from.name: Flóka-varði, 'where Hörðaland and Rogaland meet' (Bømlafjord area (?))

to.name: Flóka-vágr in Shetland (unidentified bay (?))

legs.original: Þeir hlóðu þar varða, er blótið hafði verit, ok kölluðu Flóka-varða. Þat er þar, er mœtisk Hörða-land ok Roga-land. Hann fór fyrst til Hjaltlandz, ok lá í Flóka-vági.
legs.translation: and put to sea where it is now called 'Flóka-Varði,' =Flokis beacon. There Hordaland and Rogaland meet. He went first to the to the Shetlands and lay there in Flokis Bight
legs.landmarks: a cairn (varði) raised where the sacrifice was made; Flóka-vágr in Shetland; his daughter drowned in Geirhildar-vatn
legs.scholars: Flóka-varði and Flóka-vágr are not pinned down (?).

to.name: Gata (Götu), Eysturoy, Faroes

legs.original: Flóki siglði þaðan til Færeyja, ok gipti þar dóttur sína; frá henni var Þrándr í Götu.
legs.translation: From there Floce sailed to the Faereys, and then he gave his daughter in marriage. From her is come Thrond o' Gate.
legs.landmarks: his daughter married in the Faroes; her descendant is Þrándr í Götu (of Gata)
legs.scholars: Hauksbók only (not in Sturlubók/Ellwood). Gata: sure as Þrándr's home.

to.name: Horn, east Iceland

legs.original: Þaðan siglði hann út í haf með hrafna þá þrjá, er hann hafði blótið í Noregi. Ok er hann lét lausan inn fyrsta, fló sá aptr um stafn. Annarr fló í lopt upp, ok aptr til skips; inn þriði fló fram um stafn í þá átt, er þeir fundu landit. Þeir kómu austan at Horni.
legs.translation: Floki took three ravens with him to sea. When he set free the first, it flew aft over the stem [errata: stern]; the second flew up into the air and back to the ship again; but the third flew forth straightway over the stem, in the direction in which they found the land. They hove in from the east at the Horn
legs.bearing: none; the third raven gives the bearing ('í þá átt, er þeir fundu landit')
legs.landmarks: three ravens: the first flies back (land astern), the second up and back (no land in reach), the third ahead (land ahead)
legs.scholars: Horn: likely Eystrahorn/Vesturhorn. The ravens are a story, but the raven-release check is a fine map activity (ours).

to.name: Reykjanes, with Snæfellsnes seen across Faxaflói

legs.original: Þá siglðu þeir fyrir sunnan landit. En er þeir siglðu vestr um Reykjanes, ok upp lauk firðinum, svá at þeir sá Snæfellz-nes
legs.translation: and then they coasted the land by the south. But as they sailed west round Reykjanes, and the firth opened out to them, so that they saw Snaefellness
legs.landmarks: along the south coast with the land to starboard; round Reykjanes the bay (Faxaflói) opens and Snæfellsnes comes in sight
legs.scholars: Sure.
